series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/1] mm, swap: only prefer nonfull clusters on synchronous devices
series_items.patch_summary: The patch partially reverts a previous change that preferred non-full clusters over free ones for all devices, except synchronous devices like zram. It introduces a new function `swap_prefer_free_cluster` to determine whether to prefer free clusters based on the device's flags. This is done to improve write performance by keeping swapout batches contiguous and allowing writes to be merged.

review_comments.author: Nhat Pham
review_comments.summary: Identified a potential issue with zswap and suggested adding a best-effort check for zswappability. The patch author's approach to preferring non-full clusters on synchronous devices is generally accepted, but the reviewer wonders if it should also be applied to zswap.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 8:51 AM Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr> wrote:
>
> Commit 9a42aed48421 ("mm, swap: prefer nonfull over free clusters") made
> allocations fill the nonfull clusters of their order before taking a
> free one, on every device without discard. Since commit 3cedb745d354
> ("mm: clarify the folio_free_swap() for do_swap_page()"), an exclusive
> write fault frees the swap slot, so a workload that rewrites swapped out
> memory leaves holes in full clusters, which then go back on the nonfull
> list. Reclaim allocates slots one folio at a time, so a batch of folios
> gets scattered over those holes, its writes can't be merged and it is
> written with many small requests.
>
> So partially revert commit 9a42aed48421 ("mm, swap: prefer nonfull over
> free clusters") and prefer free clusters again, except on synchronous
> devices like zram: they don't merge I/O, so the contiguity of the slots
> doesn't matter to them, and filling the holes first keeps the free
> clusters for large folios.
>
> Fixes: 9a42aed48421 ("mm, swap: prefer nonfull over free clusters")
> Suggested-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>
> Signed-off-by: Alexandre Ghiti <alex@ghiti.fr>

LGTM for the most part:

Reviewed-by: Nhat Pham <nphamcs@gmail.com>

Quick comment below:

> ---
>  mm/swapfile.c | 19 +++++++++++++------
>  1 file changed, 13 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)
>
> diff --git a/mm/swapfile.c b/mm/swapfile.c
> index 189f04d8838f..1c1b5d0b724a 100644
> --- a/mm/swapfile.c
> +++ b/mm/swapfile.c
> @@ -973,6 +973,17 @@ static bool __swap_cluster_alloc_entries(struct swap_info_struct *si,
>         return true;
>  }
>
> +/*
> + * Prefer a new cluster over a nonfull one if the device needs discard, to
> + * spread out the writes, or if it is not synchronous, to keep the slots
> + * of a swapout batch contiguous so that its writes can be merged.
> + */
> +static bool swap_prefer_free_cluster(struct swap_info_struct *si)
> +{
> +       return (si->flags & SWP_PAGE_DISCARD) ||
> +              !(si->flags & SWP_SYNCHRONOUS_IO);
> +}

Side note - I wonder if it's worth it to also prefer non-full clusters
for zswap as well?

It's a bit tricky, but I suppose you can do a best-effort check of the
folio's cgroup's zswappability?

patches_submitted.patch_summary: The patch series addresses a performance regression in Linux kernel version 7.3, which increased swap I/O requests by up to 59% on certain devices. The issue arises from the interaction between two commits: one that prefers non-full clusters over free ones and another that frees swap slots on exclusive write faults. The patch series proposes to only prefer non-full clusters on synchronous devices like zram, where filling holes first keeps free clusters available for large folios.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 07/10] drm/gem: Switch to __nonnull_args() macro
patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to standardize the use of non-null attributes across the kernel by replacing raw compiler attributes with the __nonnull_args() macro. The first patch in the series, [PATCH 07/10], specifically targets the drm/gem module and replaces __attribute__((nonnull)) with __nonnull_args(). This change is intended to keep attribute quirks in one place rather than having them scattered throughout the code.

review_comments.author: Andy Shevchenko
review_comments.summary: Initially suggested that the patch might be unnecessary, but later retracted this comment and suggested cleaning up headers that pull compiler_types/compile_attributes directly.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 02:00:28PM +0100, Miguel Ojeda wrote:
> On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32\u202fAM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
> >
> > Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?
> 
> No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
> custom with the compiler flags etc.).

Usually it comes to the mere drivers via types.h, in rare cases (usually some
more generic library headers, we do better granularity as it affects the almost
entire kernel. Just double check that types.h is explicitly included.

-- 
With Best Regards,
Andy Shevchenko

review_comments.author: Andy Shevchenko
review_comments.summary: Told the patch author to discard his previous comment, and suggested cleaning up headers that pull compiler_types/compile_attributes directly.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 01:12:06PM +0000, Dmitry Ilvokhin wrote:
> On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 02:00:28PM +0100, Miguel Ojeda wrote:
> > On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32\u202fAM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
> > >
> > > Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?
> > 
> > No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
> > custom with the compiler flags etc.).
> 
> Just to add a bit more colour to Miguel's reply.
> 
> I believe idea behind include/linux/compiler_attributes.h is to make
> attribute wrappers as simple and transparent to use as native compiler
> attributes. In particular, this means they should be available in every
> kernel compilation unit without any additional effort.
> 
> For this reason, all the nessesary plumbing is handled at the build
> machinery level (see scripts/Makefile.lib:171), where '-include'
> compiler flag is used to pull in include/linux/compiler_types.h, which
> in turn pulls include/linux/compiler_attributes.h.

Ah, TIL! Please, discard my comment then. Perhaps we need to clean up all
headers that pull compiler_types/compile_attributes directly (the same way
we do for kconfig.h).

-- 
With Best Regards,
Andy Shevchenko

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 00/10] treewide: switch to __nonnull_args() macro
patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series replaces open-coded uses of the __attribute__((nonnull)) macro with the __nonnull_args() macro, which is a wrapper that keeps the quirks of the attribute in one place. The goal is to standardize nonnull attribute usage across the Linux kernel tree. The patches can be applied separately and are build-tested on various configurations. Some instances of __attribute__((nonnull)) remain in the tools subdirectory and should be updated separately after this patchset lands.

Avoid kernel-doc warnings by supporting __nonnull_args()
as a function transform.

This is a preparatory change for the treewide migration from
__attribute__((nonnull)) to __nonnull_args() macro.

Signed-off-by: Dmitry Ilvokhin <d@ilvokhin.com>

 tools/lib/python/kdoc/xforms_lists.py | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/tools/lib/python/kdoc/xforms_lists.py b/tools/lib/python/kdoc/xforms_lists.py
index 320f977c5bac..a8c47ede8637 100644
--- a/tools/lib/python/kdoc/xforms_lists.py
+++ b/tools/lib/python/kdoc/xforms_lists.py
@@ -108,6 +108,7 @@ class CTransforms:
         (CMatch("__attribute__"), ""),
         (CMatch("STATIC_IFN_KUNIT"), ""),
         (CMatch("INLINE_IFN_KUNIT"), ""),
+        (CMatch("__nonnull_args"), ""),
 
         #
         # HACK: this is similar to process_export() hack. It is meant to

Commit 22302af28d3f ("cleanup: Annotate guard constructors with
nonnull") added the macro __nonnull_args() to wrap raw compiler
attribute.

Replace __attribute__((nonnull)) with __nonnull_args() to
standardize nonnull attribute usage across the tree and keep the
attribute's quirks in one place rather than open-coded at every call
site.

Add spaces after the commas in the __nonnull_args() argument list to
follow the usual coding style (according to checkpatch).

-__attribute__((nonnull(2,3)))

 {
@@ -45,7 +45,7 @@ static struct list_head *merge(void *priv, list_cmp_func_t cmp,
  * prev-link restoration pass, or maintaining the prev links

-__attribute__((nonnull(2,3,4,5)))
+__nonnull_args(2, 3, 4, 5)
 static void merge_final(void *priv, list_cmp_func_t cmp, struct list_head *head,

 {
@@ -175,7 +175,7 @@ static void merge_final(void *priv, list_cmp_func_t cmp, struct list_head *head,
  * of size 2^k varies from 2^(k-1) (cases 3 and 5 when x == 0) to
  * 2^(k+1) - 1 (second merge of case 5 when x == 2^(k-1) - 1).

-__attribute__((nonnull(2,3)))
+__nonnull_args(2, 3)

 {
 	struct list_head *list = head->next, *pending = NULL;

tools/testing/shared/linux/xarray.h directly includes the kernel's
include/linux/xarray.h, which now uses __nonnull_args(). The macro is
not defined under tools/, breaking test builds.

-		unsigned long max, xa_mark_t) __attribute__((nonnull(2)));
+		unsigned long max, xa_mark_t) __nonnull_args(2);

-		unsigned long max, xa_mark_t) __attribute__((nonnull(2)));
+		unsigned long max, xa_mark_t) __nonnull_args(2);

 		unsigned long max, unsigned int n, xa_mark_t);

diff --git a/tools/include/linux/compiler.h b/tools/include/linux/compiler.h
index 03ecf9086643..fad2c6131a80 100644
--- a/tools/include/linux/compiler.h
+++ b/tools/include/linux/compiler.h
@@ -68,6 +68,10 @@
 #define __naked __attribute__((__naked__))
 #endif
 
+#ifndef __nonnull_args
+#define __nonnull_args(x...) __attribute__((__nonnull__(x)))
+#endif
+
 /* Are two types/vars the same type (ignoring qualifiers)? */
 #ifndef __same_type
 # define __same_type(a, b) __builtin_types_compatible_p(typeof(a), typeof(b))

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 02:00:28PM +0100, Miguel Ojeda wrote:
> On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32\u202fAM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
> >
> > Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?
> 
> No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
> custom with the compiler flags etc.).

Just to add a bit more colour to Miguel's reply.

I believe idea behind include/linux/compiler_attributes.h is to make
attribute wrappers as simple and transparent to use as native compiler
attributes. In particular, this means they should be available in every
kernel compilation unit without any additional effort.

For this reason, all the nessesary plumbing is handled at the build
machinery level (see scripts/Makefile.lib:171), where '-include'
compiler flag is used to pull in include/linux/compiler_types.h, which
in turn pulls include/linux/compiler_attributes.h.

review_comments.author: Andy Shevchenko

review_comments.raw_body:
On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 02:00:28PM +0100, Miguel Ojeda wrote:
> On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32\u202fAM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
> >
> > Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?
> 
> No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
> custom with the compiler flags etc.).

Usually it comes to the mere drivers via types.h, in rare cases (usually some
more generic library headers, we do better granularity as it affects the almost
entire kernel. Just double check that types.h is explicitly included.

-- 
With Best Regards,
Andy Shevchenko

---

On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 01:12:06PM +0000, Dmitry Ilvokhin wrote:
> On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 02:00:28PM +0100, Miguel Ojeda wrote:
> > On Thu, Oct 29, 2026 at 8:32\u202fAM Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de> wrote:
> > >
> > > Should gem.h now include <linux/compiler_attributes.h> ?
> > 
> > No, it should be included for you (unless you are doing something
> > custom with the compiler flags etc.).
> 
> Just to add a bit more colour to Miguel's reply.
> 
> I believe idea behind include/linux/compiler_attributes.h is to make
> attribute wrappers as simple and transparent to use as native compiler
> attributes. In particular, this means they should be available in every
> kernel compilation unit without any additional effort.
> 
> For this reason, all the nessesary plumbing is handled at the build
> machinery level (see scripts/Makefile.lib:171), where '-include'
> compiler flag is used to pull in include/linux/compiler_types.h, which
> in turn pulls include/linux/compiler_attributes.h.

Ah, TIL! Please, discard my comment then. Perhaps we need to clean up all
headers that pull compiler_types/compile_attributes directly (the same way
we do for kconfig.h).

-- 
With Best Regards,
Andy Shevchenko
